sourcedFrom: CVA Scout Owner's Manual — No. 32380 • Rev. 07/26 (not printed (the edition code reads Rev. 07/26))
cleanIntro: CVA's own cleaning procedure for the Scout, from the one book CVA prints for every Scout. The Scout is a single-shot break-action: the breeching lever opens it, the barrel pivots forward, and the bore is cleaned from the breech end. Taking the forend off is part of the routine clean. Driving the pivot pin to take the barrel off, and servicing the firing pin, are occasional jobs the book saves for a wet or misbehaving gun, so they are in the Deep Clean. The Scout TD's take-down section is a different gun's procedure and is not used here.

steps.title: Breeching lever back, barrel forward, look through it
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, pull the breeching lever to the rear and let the barrel pivot forward. Look into the chamber and through the bore and confirm both are empty and unobstructed before anything else happens.
steps.prose: On the Scout the breeching lever sits at the rear of the trigger guard and you pull it back, usually with your trigger finger. The book does not say where the Scout XP's lever sits, so find the lever on your own rifle rather than assuming. With the barrel pivoted forward you can see straight down the bore from the breech, and that is the only check that proves the gun is empty.
steps.quote: Verify that the barrel is unloaded before you begin by pulling the breeching lever to the rear, pivoting the barrel forward and visually inspecting to see that the barrel is unloaded and unobstructed.
steps.cite: CVA Scout Owner's Manual — No. 32380 • Rev. 07/26 — CLEANING THE CVA Scout, step 1, PDF p.8 (the book prints no folios)
steps.warn: Always wear eye protection. Flying debris from the breech area and muzzle are common with any firearm.

steps.title: The extractor lifts the case; your fingers take it out
steps.action: If a case or cartridge is in the chamber, pivot the barrel forward until it stops. The extractor lifts the rim clear of the chamber, and you take the case out by its rear with your fingers.
steps.prose: The Scout does not throw the case. The extractor only partly withdraws it, so check the chamber by eye and pull the case out by hand and set it away from the bench before you go on.
steps.quote: Note that the extractor only partially pulls the case from the chamber, it does not eject it.
steps.cite: CVA Scout Owner's Manual — No. 32380 • Rev. 07/26 — LOADING AND FIRING THE CVA Scout, step 6, PDF p.8

steps.title: Unscrew the forend and take it off
steps.action: With the gun confirmed empty, unscrew the forend and lift it off the barrel.
steps.prose: On the basic Scout the forend is held to the barrel by one or two screws. The book does not say how the Scout XP's forend is held, so look before you turn anything. With the forend off, the routine strip is complete. Taking the barrel off the pivot pin is a separate job that the book reserves for a gun that has been wet, so it is in the Deep Clean.
steps.cite: CVA Scout Owner's Manual — No. 32380 • Rev. 07/26 — CLEANING THE CVA Scout, step 3, PDF p.8

steps.title: Clean from the breech end
steps.action: Use a good cleaning rod and jag and work from the breech end of the barrel, with the barrel pivoted open.
steps.prose: The breech-end rule protects the muzzle crown. A rod that rubs the crown can damage the last edge the bullet touches, and accuracy suffers.
steps.quote: CVA recommends that you clean from the breech end of the barrel to protect the muzzle crown.
steps.cite: CVA Scout Owner's Manual — No. 32380 • Rev. 07/26 — CLEANING THE CVA Scout, step 2, PDF p.8

steps.title: Wet bore brush, full-length strokes, let it soak
steps.action: Wet a properly fitting bore brush with solvent and brush the barrel with several full-length strokes. Leave the solvent in the bore for a few minutes, following the solvent maker's directions.
steps.prose: A full-length stroke means the brush travels the whole bore each time. The soak is part of the step: the solvent does the work while the bore sits.
steps.quote: Using a properly fitting bore brush that is wet with solvent, brush the barrel with several full-length strokes.
steps.cite: CVA Scout Owner's Manual — No. 32380 • Rev. 07/26 — CLEANING THE CVA Scout, step 4, PDF p.8

steps.title: Dry patches until they come out clean
steps.action: Push clean, dry patches through the barrel to lift out the fouling and solvent. Repeat the solvent and the patches until a dry patch comes out clean.
steps.prose: The clean dry patch is the finish line the book sets. Stopping before it leaves solvent and loosened fouling in the bore.
steps.quote: Push clean, dry patches through the barrel to remove fouling and solvent. Repeat the solvent and patching process until the dry patches come out clean.
steps.cite: CVA Scout Owner's Manual — No. 32380 • Rev. 07/26 — CLEANING THE CVA Scout, step 4, PDF p.9
steps.warn: Always use proper cleaning procedures. Firing of an improperly maintained or corroded firearm may lead to unsafe pressure conditions and/or cause the barrel to rupture resulting in severe injury or death.

steps.title: Oil the bore, the pivot pin and the outside
steps.action: Finish with a light coat of oil in the bore, on the pivot pin and over the exterior of the gun.
steps.prose: The book names the pivot pin right after the bore. It is the hinge the whole action turns on, and the oil is there to keep corrosion off it.
steps.quote: Oil the bore, pivot pin and exterior of the gun to prevent corrosion
steps.cite: CVA Scout Owner's Manual — No. 32380 • Rev. 07/26 — CLEANING THE CVA Scout, step 6, PDF p.9

steps.title: ⛔ CVA's serial-number recall, printed in this book
steps.action: This book carries CVA's 1997 voluntary recall. It covers CVA in-line muzzleloading models whose serial numbers end in -95 or -96, not the Scout, which is a cartridge break-action. If you own any CVA in-line muzzleloader, read its serial number and check it now.
steps.prose: ⛔ By CVA's own words a recalled gun must not be used or lent to anyone, and CVA asks owners to call them for a replacement. It is repeated here because the notice is printed in the Scout's book, and the Scout may not be the only CVA in the safe.
steps.aside: Example of a recalled serial number: 61-13-xxxxxx-95
steps.quote: If you, or someone you know, have a CVA in-line firearm with such a serial number, do not use or allow anyone else to use to gun under any circumstances.
steps.cite: CVA Scout Owner's Manual — No. 32380 • Rev. 07/26 — VOLUNTARY RECALL INFORMATION, PDF p.11

deepSteps.title: Barrel off: drive out the pivot pin (wet guns)
deepSteps.action: With the forend off, drive the pivot pin out with a soft brass or aluminium punch and lift the barrel away from the frame.
deepSteps.prose: CVA treats this as an occasional job, not a routine one. Do it when the gun has been out in rain or has been wet. The book specifies a soft punch, brass or aluminium, so the pin and the frame are not marked. This is the Scout and Scout XP procedure only: the Scout TD comes apart by its own take-down system.
deepSteps.quote: To remove the barrel, drive out the pivot pin with a soft punch (brass or aluminum). This step is not always necessary but should be performed if the gun has been exposed to rain or water. Does not apply to Take Down model.
deepSteps.cite: CVA Scout Owner's Manual — No. 32380 • Rev. 07/26 — CLEANING THE CVA Scout, step 3, PDF p.8

deepSteps.title: Firing pin: only when it needs it
deepSteps.action: Service the firing pin only occasionally, or when the mechanism is malfunctioning or has been soaked with water. A firing pin that will not retract in the function check is the sign that it needs this.
deepSteps.prose: The firing pin is the one internal part the book takes you into. It stops at the firing pin and its spring, and so does this guide.
deepSteps.quote: This step is needed only occasionally or if the mechanism is malfunctioning or soaked with water.
deepSteps.cite: CVA Scout Owner's Manual — No. 32380 • Rev. 07/26 — CLEANING THE CVA Scout, step 5, PDF p.9

deepSteps.title: Cock the hammer to expose the firing pin
deepSteps.action: Confirm again that the gun is unloaded, then cock the hammer. Cocking it exposes the rear of the firing pin and the screw above it.
deepSteps.prose: The book repeats the unloaded check at the start of this job, so repeat it.
deepSteps.quote: Cock the hammer to expose the rear of the firing pin
deepSteps.cite: CVA Scout Owner's Manual — No. 32380 • Rev. 07/26 — CLEANING THE CVA Scout, step 5, PDF p.9

deepSteps.title: Remove the screw above the firing pin
deepSteps.action: Take out the screw above the firing pin. The firing pin and its spring come out after it. Clean and lightly oil them, then put them back in reverse order.
deepSteps.prose: Have a tray ready: the book says the pin and spring come out with the screw, and both are small. The book ends this procedure at the pin and spring, and nothing deeper is published.
deepSteps.quote: The firing pin and spring will follow. Reassemble in reverse order.
deepSteps.cite: CVA Scout Owner's Manual — No. 32380 • Rev. 07/26 — CLEANING THE CVA Scout, step 5, PDF p.9

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retract test, after servicing
deepSteps.action: With the barrel pivoted open, pull the trigger to the rear and push the hammer forward with your thumb. The firing pin should stand out from the face of the receiver. Let go of the hammer and the trigger, and the pin should pull back into the receiver by itself.
deepSteps.prose: A firing pin that stays proud of the receiver face is the fault this test exists to find. Service it and test again. If it still will not retract, the book sends you to CVA rather than further into the gun.
deepSteps.quote: If the firing pin fails to retract it should be serviced and cleaned as described in the cleaning section. Repeat this test after servicing. If the firing pin still does not retract automatically contact CVA Customer Service.
deepSteps.cite: CVA Scout Owner's Manual — No. 32380 • Rev. 07/26 — LOADING AND FIRING THE CVA Scout, step 2, PDF p.8

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Clean from the breech end with the barrel pivoted open
Wet, properly fitting bore brush, several full-length strokes; let the solvent soak a few minutes
Dry patches until they come out clean

cleaning.name: ACTION & EXTERIOR
tasks: Light oil over the exterior to prevent corrosion

reassembly: If the firing pin was out, put the firing pin and spring back and refit the screw above it, in reverse order of removal.
If the barrel came off, it goes back in reverse: barrel on the frame, the oiled pivot pin back in with the soft punch. The book gives no further instruction for it.
Refit the forend and tighten its screws.
Close the action and run the firing pin check before the gun goes away.
fncheck: With the gun unloaded and the barrel pivoted forward, pull the trigger to the rear and push the hammer forward with your thumb: the firing pin should stand out from the face of the receiver. Let go of the hammer and the trigger, and it should pull back in by itself. If it does not, service the firing pin (Deep Clean) and test again; if it still does not retract, contact CVA.
breakOpen: pull the breeching lever to the rear and let the barrel pivot forward.
